en-US.description:
pew2 lets you drive the coding agents already running on your computer from your phone, and talk to them hands-free.

You install a small command line tool on your Mac, Windows or Linux machine, scan a code once, and the agents on that machine show up in the app. Send a message, watch the work happen live, answer a question when it asks one, and approve or reject the changes it wants to make. Your computer runs the agent; your phone shows its work.

TALK TO PEW, HANDS-FREE
Out on a walk or a run? Call Pew, the AI voice assistant, and ask what your agents are doing, send one a task, or answer an approval by voice. If you allow it, Pew can ring you like a phone call when a conversation you chose is stuck waiting on you, and only then. Voice calls run on OpenAI using an OpenAI login you already have or add once; the app asks before the first call.

WORKS WITH THE AGENTS YOU ALREADY USE
pew2 speaks the Agent Client Protocol, so it works with a long list of agents rather than one. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot, Cline, Qwen Code, goose, Cursor and more are supported out of the box. If you have none installed, pew2 tells you exactly what to run.

ENCRYPTED SESSION TRAFFIC
Everything between your phone and your computer is encrypted end to end with XChaCha20-Poly1305. The key is created when you pair and never leaves your two devices. Away from home the traffic passes through a relay that only sees encrypted data. You can run your own relay if you prefer.

NO ACCOUNT, NO ANALYTICS
There is no sign up, no analytics, no crash reporting and no advertising. Your computer holds the agent's history. Notifications and call rings pass through Expo, Apple and the relay with a short summary that is not end to end encrypted, and voice calls go to OpenAI; the privacy policy explains exactly what each one carries.

OPEN SOURCE
The app, the command line tool and the relay are AGPL-3.0 at github.com/KenKaiii/pew2.

REQUIRES A COMPUTER
pew2 is a remote control, so it needs the free pew2 command line tool running on a computer you own. Installing it is one command.
en-US.promoText: Start a task at your desk, follow it from the sofa, or talk it through with Pew on a run. Your coding agents, in your pocket.

en-US.releaseNotes: New: talk to Pew, an AI voice assistant, about your agents, hands-free. Pew can ring you when a conversation you choose needs you. A new home screen with your latest sessions, smoother chats, and faster opening of long conversations.

review.notes:
WHAT THIS APP IS
pew2 is a remote control for coding agents that run on your own computer: the phone half of a two part tool. The other half is a free command line program installed on a Mac, Windows or Linux machine with one command. No accounts or hosted conversation database; an optional relay forwards encrypted traffic, and notifications use Expo and Apple.

WHY THE APP SHOWS A PAIRING SCREEN ON FIRST LAUNCH
The app asks you to scan a pairing code made by the command line program on the user's own computer. Without one running there is nothing to connect to, as a TV remote does nothing without a TV. This is intended, not a defect or a paywall.

HOW TO TEST IT
The fastest path, on any Mac, takes about a minute:

1. Open Terminal and run:
     curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KenKaiii/pew2/main/install.sh | sh
2. Run:
     pew2 setup
   It finds any coding agents already installed, starts a local service, and prints a QR code.
3. Open pew2 on the device, tap Pair, and scan that QR code.

The app then shows that computer's agents. With none installed, step 2 prints the command to install one. If you would prefer a machine already running so only step 3 is needed, reply to this note and one will be provided with a pairing code.

ENCRYPTION
Phone to computer traffic is end to end encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305 (@noble/ciphers, and Apple CryptoKit on iOS): standard cryptography only, none proprietary. Off the local network it passes through a relay that only sees ciphertext.

PERMISSIONS
Camera is for scanning the pairing code and for taking a photo to send to an agent. Photos is for attaching an image and saving one an agent returns. Microphone is for dictating a message (speech recognition, on device) and for voice calls with Pew (audio goes to OpenAI during a call, after the user agrees). Notifications say when an agent has finished or needs an answer; the computer sends them through Expo to APNs, and Expo and Apple handle the project or agent name, a short excerpt, a session identifier and a delivery address (not end to end encrypted). Prompts and attachments go to the user's chosen agent over the encrypted connection; agent providers have their own data practices. The privacy policy and terms are reachable before pairing and in the connection sheet.

VOICE CALLS WITH PEW (AI)
Pew is an AI voice assistant (OpenAI Realtime). Before the first call the app shows "Pew is an AI. Your voice goes to OpenAI." with an "Agree and call" button (guideline 5.1.2(i)); the call screen labels it "Pew · AI" and Pew says it is an AI if asked. During a call the user's voice and a briefing about their own sessions go to OpenAI. No audio is recorded; the user's own computer keeps the text of the last 20 exchanges per conversation (so a later call carries on), never sent to the developer, deleted after 30 days or with "Forget call history". The call uses the user's own OpenAI login from their computer (a 10 minute key is minted per call).

CALL-STYLE RINGS (PushKit / CallKit)
Optional, off by default. Pew rings the user like a phone call only when (1) they switched "Ring me" on (1 hour, 3 hours or until stopped) and (2) an agent is stopped waiting on them (an approval or question), in any chat or only chosen ones, as they set; or (3) they asked Pew to call back. Every VoIP push is reported to CallKit; the computer decides whether to ring before sending, so no silent VoIP pushes are sent. Calls are not added to Recents. CallKit is disabled for China storefront users (a notification is shown instead). To see a ring: pair, open the connection sheet, tap "Calls · Settings", choose "1 hour" under Ring me, then ask an agent to do something that needs approval and lock the phone (about 90 seconds). Or call Pew and say "call me back in 30 seconds".

SOURCE CODE
The entire app, command line tool and relay are open source under AGPL-3.0 at https://github.com/KenKaiii/pew2 if anything needs verifying.
